A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LLaRA work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across revisions and renumbering.

before.justification: v2.pdf reports original VIMA simulation experiments, xArm robot evaluations, and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3.pdf retains those original experiments and adds evaluations of language descriptions, baseline variants, action failures, and unseen real-world tasks.

M1.justification: Appendix A.1.3 adds D-inBC (L), replacing coordinate-based reference-image descriptions with natural language. Qwen2-VL generates training descriptions, while LLaRA generates descriptions during inference. This extends the input-processing procedure; the original architecture, action representation, and six auxiliary tasks remain.

E1.justification: The original datasets remain, but v3 substantially extends test requirements: T5–T7 involve selecting yellow objects, identifying baked goods, and placing healthy food near an animal (Appendix C.4). Appendix B.9 also introduces a VIMA environment that randomly ignores actions, adding an execution-failure scenario.

E2.justification: v3 adds RT-2 Style (2R) and RT-2 Style + Aux (D) to the VIMA-8k comparisons (Tables 3 and 16). The real-world finetuning and joint-training comparisons also gain inBC + Aux (D), previously evaluated there only in zero-shot mode. These extend the existing comparator families.

E3.justification: The reported T2 rotation selection changes from a 0–180-degree range to {30, 90, 120, 180}; the PDFs do not establish whether existing experiments were rerun. v3 also introduces an average across L1–L3, real-world evaluations of the 660k-pretrained RT-2 baseline, and the action-suppression testing procedure.

E4.justification: New analyses test natural-language versus structured reference descriptions, rotation-token precision, auxiliary-data benefits for RT-2, recovery under ignored actions, and semantic generalization (Appendices A.1.3, B.8–B.9, and C.4). These substantially broaden the explanations and robustness properties examined beyond the retained ablations.

E5.justification: Appendix C.4 newly specifies 10 randomly initialized evaluation episodes per task for T5–T7. The existing simulation protocol retains 20 seeds and the original real-world protocol retains 20 episodes; this is not evidence of changed repetition counts for those experiments. Neither version reports confidence intervals or training-run variability.

E6.justification: Original raw simulation rows and headline scores are retained, but substantial new results appear. Examples include RT-2 Style + Aux (D) scoring 36.9/35.8/32.1 on VIMA-8k, failure-condition scores of 87.7/86.2/75.8, and reported T5–T7 scores of 60/55/50. D-inBC (L) and additional real-world training combinations also gain results. These are new conditions and entries, not same-setting gains over v2.

T1.justification: The MDP formulation, history-conditioned policy definition, and mathematical action representation are retained. Neither version introduces theoretical results or proofs, and v3 adds no substantive formal derivation.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain conversation-formatted behavior cloning, image-coordinate actions, and self-supervised auxiliary data for efficient robot learning. v3 foregrounds VLM-to-VLA transfer and preserved generalization, but these claims already appear in v2, including its introduction, conclusion, and Section 6.2.

C2.justification: v3 discusses potential unfairness from the original rotation-token resolution and explains RT-2's data demands through learning new token semantics. It also attributes confusion on the new semantic tasks to the 7B language model's capacity. The substantive limitations in Appendix D remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 documents the Qwen2-VL-7B-Instruct checkpoint and description-generation prompt, the two-token rotation encoding, and the GPT-4o version used. Existing optimizer settings, batch sizes, robot hardware, dataset-construction details, and code/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: Qwen2-VL and TraceVLA are newly cited, with TraceVLA included among concurrent VLA approaches. Comparisons with PALM-E and SpatialVLM are shortened, while the positioning around image-coordinate actions and auxiliary-data generation remains.

P1.justification: The abstract is rewritten, related work is condensed, and selected introduction, method, and conclusion passages are edited. New appendix subsections and conference headers are added, but the overall narrative structure and most existing appendix prose and prompt templates remain.

P2.justification: Figures 1–4 are redesigned. Figure 5 gains an average-success panel and displays full-dataset baseline results already tabulated in v2; other plot axes and example color coding are revised. New tables, an expanded real-world comparison, and a transposed generalization table substantially change the presentation beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: The added baseline controls address alternative explanations for the performance gap, while failure and semantic-generalization tests strengthen the existing empirical case. Redesigned diagrams also clarify the procedure. The gain is qualified by a new reporting inconsistency: Appendix C.4 specifies 10 episodes per task, but Table 20 reports 55% for T6 without explaining the aggregation. Overall, v3 provides useful additional validation with a limited net quality improvement.
